rootCause: IlGenerator.GenerateIl indexed `instructionMap[target][0]` for a branch target without checking the list was non-empty. rootCause: IlGenerator drops a `.ctor` call outside a constructor, on the grounds that C# cannot call a constructor on an object that already exists and the object is constructed at the `newobj` already. That is true of a reference type and false of a value type: there is no allocation to fuse with, il2cpp calls the constructor on the address of the slot holding the value, and that is exactly what C# compiles `x = new T(...)` to. The receiver load in the same case already emits the address for a value type, so not dropping the call is all that was needed.

observed: 146 CS1061 in Assembly-CSharp naming a private field of a framework generic: 68 `List<T>._version`, 35 `_items`, 34 `_size`, 7 `bool.m_value`, 2 `_syncRoot`.
expected: nothing better is available - see the root cause
rootCause: Measured rather than assumed. The read side of the trivial-accessor pairing already covers `_size`: all 34 of its occurrences in Assembly-CSharp are *writes* (`list._size = num`), and `List<T>.Count` has no public setter, so there is nothing to pair with. `_items` is 35 reads and 0 writes, and `List<T>` has no public property returning `T[]` - the nearest is the indexer, which takes an argument the field access does not have. `_version` is an enumeration-invalidation counter with no public surface at all. So every one of these is il2cpp having inlined the body of `List<T>.Add` or an enumerator into the caller, and the assembly the export compiles against is the real `List<T>`, which has no public way to say what the recovered body does. The export is faithful and the compiler is right to reject it. Fixing it would mean expressing the inlined body as the call it was inlined from, which is a different and much larger problem than accessor pairing.

observed: a load off a generic type's `this` reported as unresolved and then `(List<T>)0`; 1123 loads classified as 'generic instance, value type argument' or 'reference arguments'.
rootCause: GenericInstanceFieldLayout bailed if any base type had an instance field, and GetSizeAndAlignment returned null for a user-defined value type, truncating the layout at the first struct field. Both were marked TODO. Fixed by walking the whole base chain - and every base, not only one that declares fields, since ArgumentException's immediate base declares none and Exception above it declares 0x80 - and by taking a struct's size from il2cpp's recorded instance_size less the object header, which is exact where packing its fields is a guess.

rootCause: The compiler computes a field's address ahead of the load whenever it is wanted more than once, and nothing typed the intermediate - so the load off it did not resolve, and neither did the load off what it produced. [t + K] where t = base + J is [base + (J + K)]; folding it presents the base and addend the machine really used and lets ResolveFieldOffsets validate as it always did. Must run inside the type fixpoint, because it needs the base typed and what it produces types the next base - the same place ArrayRecovery.RecoverComputedAccesses runs for an element.

generatedFile: Assets/Scripts/Assembly-CSharp/DataController.cs, and 174 static-storage loads across the export
observed: `gpc.<field>` read as `[Il2CppStaticFields<UnityEngine.Quaternion>+3C]` - 69 occurrences in one file - which is past the end of a block sixteen bytes long, with every use of the value typed from that.
expected: the field of GamePlayController at that offset
rootCause: PropagatePhi's forward rule took the first typed input and stopped, so a merge of two unrelated values was typed as whichever the operand order put first. The ISIL says it outright: `Phi v308 (Il2CppStaticFields<UnityEngine.Quaternion>), v644 (Il2CppStaticFields<UnityEngine.Quaternion>), v582 (GamePlayController)`. The compiler reuses a scratch register freely and X8 carries both a class's static field storage and ordinary objects, so this shape is routine. The backward rule then spread the wrong type to the phi's other inputs.
evidence: stage dump 005-after ResolveTypesAndFields: the phi with two disagreeing input types
Quaternion declares one static field of sixteen bytes, so offset 0x3C cannot be one of its statics
